literal: without speaking by looking intention he who knows always unchanging water to the world ornament
translation: He who knows another's intention just by looking, without a word being spoken, is an everlasting ornament to this world surrounded by the unceasing sea.
modern: ஒருவர் வாய்திறந்து சொல்லாமலேயே, அவரது முகத்தை நோக்கி அவரது குறிப்பை அறியும் ஆற்றல் உடையவன், வற்றாத கடலால் சூழப்பட்ட இந்த உலகத்திற்கு எப்போதும் ஒரு அணிகலன் ஆவான்.
explanation: This couplet praises the rare ability to read minds. A person who can understand what another is thinking merely by looking at them, without needing any words to be spoken, possesses a profound skill. The poet describes such a person as a permanent jewel to the earth, which is bounded by the ever-present ocean. The phrase 'māṟā nīr' refers to the unchanging, unceasing waters of the sea that surround the world, emphasizing the enduring value of such an insightful person.
